# Dialog

The `Dialog` component provides a modal dialog with a compound component API. It is backed by Base UI's Dialog primitive.

## Import

```tsx
import { Dialog } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";
```

The runnable examples also import `useState` from `react`, and `Button`, `Field`, `Form`, and `Text` from `@tailor-platform/app-shell`.

## Basic Usage

<example-preview name="basic-usage"></example-preview>

```tsx
function BasicUsage() {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root>
      <Dialog.Trigger render={<Button />}>Open</Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Content>
        <Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Title>Confirm Action</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description>Are you sure you want to proceed?</Dialog.Description>
        </Dialog.Header>
        <Dialog.Footer>
          <Dialog.Close render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</Dialog.Close>
          <Button>Confirm</Button>
        </Dialog.Footer>
      </Dialog.Content>
    </Dialog.Root>
  );
}
```

## Sub-components

| Sub-component        | Description                                                             |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Dialog.Root`        | Manages open/close state                                                |
| `Dialog.Trigger`     | Element that opens the dialog when clicked                              |
| `Dialog.Content`     | The main dialog panel (includes overlay and close button automatically) |
| `Dialog.Header`      | Layout wrapper for title and description                                |
| `Dialog.Body`        | Scrollable middle section; long content scrolls here, not off-screen    |
| `Dialog.Footer`      | Layout wrapper for action buttons                                       |
| `Dialog.Title`       | Dialog title (announced by screen readers)                              |
| `Dialog.Description` | Additional context below the title                                      |
| `Dialog.Close`       | Button that closes the dialog                                           |

## Props

### Dialog.Root Props

| Prop           | Type                      | Default | Description                       |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------- |
| `open`         | `boolean`                 | -       | Controlled open state             |
| `defaultOpen`  | `boolean`                 | `false` | Initial open state (uncontrolled) |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` | -       | Callback when open state changes  |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                 | `true`  | Whether the dialog is modal       |
| `children`     | `React.ReactNode`         | -       | Dialog sub-components             |

### Dialog.Content Props

| Prop   | Type                           | Default | Description                                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` | `"md"`  | Max width of the panel: 24rem, 32rem, 45rem or 60rem — the same steps as `Sheet.Content` `size` |

Also accepts `className` and all standard HTML `<div>` props. The panel never grows taller than the viewport; put long content in `Dialog.Body` so it scrolls while the header and footer stay in view.

## Tall Content

`Dialog.Content` is never taller than the viewport minus 2rem (16px above and below, the same margin as on the sides). Without a `Dialog.Body`, content that is taller makes the whole dialog scroll, including the title and the close button. `Escape` and a click on the backdrop still close it.

On open, focus moves to the first control in the dialog. In a dialog that scrolls, this happens only when that control is in view at the top. When it is below the fold (for example, a footer button after a long body), the dialog itself takes focus instead, so it opens at the top rather than scrolled to that control. `Tab` then moves to the control. Pass `initialFocus` to choose the element yourself.

To keep the header and footer in view while only the middle scrolls, wrap the middle in `Dialog.Body`. `Dialog.Content` is already a flex column, and `Dialog.Body` is the only child that shrinks; the header, footer and anything else placed directly in `Dialog.Content` keep their height. A `className` with its own `max-h-*` or `overflow-*` replaces the defaults.

### Dialog.Trigger / Dialog.Close Props

Accept a `render` prop for custom element rendering (Base UI render pattern), plus standard button props.

## Controlled Usage

<example-preview name="controlled"></example-preview>

```tsx
function Controlled() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Open Dialog
      </Button>
      <Dialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Dialog.Content>
          <Dialog.Header>
            <Dialog.Title>Settings</Dialog.Title>
          </Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Footer>
            <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Done</Button>
          </Dialog.Footer>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog.Root>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Examples

### Delete Confirmation

Open the confirmation and cancel to keep the order, or confirm to remove it from this local example. No server data is changed. **Restore demo order** makes the example repeatable.

<example-preview name="delete-confirmation"></example-preview>

```tsx
function DeleteConfirmation() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [deleted, setDeleted] = useState(false);

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Text.p role="status">{deleted ? "Demo order deleted." : "Demo order: ORD-1001"}</Text.p>
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Dialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
          <Dialog.Trigger disabled={deleted} render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>
            Delete demo order
          </Dialog.Trigger>
          <Dialog.Content>
            <Dialog.Header>
              <Dialog.Title>Delete demo order?</Dialog.Title>
              <Dialog.Description>
                Remove ORD-1001 from this local example. No server data is changed.
              </Dialog.Description>
            </Dialog.Header>
            <Dialog.Footer>
              <Dialog.Close render={<Button type="button" variant="outline" />}>
                Cancel
              </Dialog.Close>
              <Button
                type="button"
                variant="destructive"
                onClick={() => {
                  setDeleted(true);
                  setOpen(false);
                }}
              >
                Delete order
              </Button>
            </Dialog.Footer>
          </Dialog.Content>
        </Dialog.Root>
        <Button
          type="button"
          variant="outline"
          disabled={!deleted}
          onClick={() => setDeleted(false)}
        >
          Restore demo order
        </Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Form Dialog

Put the `Form` inside `Dialog.Body` and submit it from the footer with `form="<id>"`, so the Save button stays visible however long the form gets. [`FormLayout`](./form-layout.md) lays the fields out in columns that fit the dialog's width.

In this example, empty or whitespace-only names are rejected through `Form` and `Field`. Cancel or close leaves the saved name unchanged; reopening restores it. Cancel is explicitly `type="button"` so it does not submit the form.

<example-preview name="form-dialog"></example-preview>

```tsx
function FormDialog() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [name, setName] = useState("Small carton");

  return (
    <div className="space-y-3">
      <Text.p role="status">Saved item name: {name}</Text.p>
      <Dialog.Root open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Dialog.Trigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit item</Dialog.Trigger>
        <Dialog.Content size="lg">
          <Dialog.Header>
            <Dialog.Title>Edit item</Dialog.Title>
            <Dialog.Description>
              Save a new name, or cancel to keep the saved name.
            </Dialog.Description>
          </Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Body>
            <Form<{ name: string; sku: string }>
              id="edit-item-form"
              noValidate
              onFormSubmit={(values) => {
                setName(values.name.trim());
                setOpen(false);
              }}
            >
              <FormLayout columns={2}>
                <Field.Root
                  name="name"
                  validate={(value) =>
                    typeof value === "string" && value.trim() ? undefined : "Name is required."
                  }
                >
                  <Field.Label required>Item name</Field.Label>
                  <Field.Control defaultValue={name} required />
                  <Field.Error>Name is required.</Field.Error>
                </Field.Root>
                <Field.Root name="sku">
                  <Field.Label>SKU</Field.Label>
                  <Field.Control defaultValue="CTN-S-01" />
                </Field.Root>
              </FormLayout>
            </Form>
          </Dialog.Body>
          <Dialog.Footer>
            <Dialog.Close render={<Button type="button" variant="outline" />}>Cancel</Dialog.Close>
            <Button type="submit" form="edit-item-form">
              Save item
            </Button>
          </Dialog.Footer>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog.Root>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Stacking

`Dialog` renders through a portal to the end of `body`, in the portal band (`--z-portal`). A menu, select or combobox opened inside the dialog renders above it, because it was opened later. A toast is always above the dialog. See [Styling and Theming → Z-index](../concepts/styling-theming.md#z-index).

A dialog may open on top of another dialog, or on top of a sheet. Keep to these limits:

- **Two levels at most.** The second dialog is for a confirmation or a warning only: a confirm before discarding changes, or a picker opened from a form dialog.
- **A third level is a step inside the dialog.** A screen that needs one changes the content of the second dialog instead of opening another.
- **Render the second dialog inside the first one's content.** The first dialog then knows that a dialog is open above it. `Escape` and a press outside close only the top dialog, and the dialog below stays open.
- When the second dialog closes and the first stays open, focus returns to the element that opened the second one.

The limits are a guideline. The component does not enforce them.

A runnable example of a confirm dialog on top of a form dialog is in [Modal Form → Second Level](../patterns/form-modal.md#second-level-confirm-or-pick).

## Accessibility

- Dialog title is announced by screen readers via `Dialog.Title`
- Focus is trapped inside the dialog while open
- Pressing `Escape` closes the dialog
- The close button is always present inside `Dialog.Content`
